question.text: For an offshore fund investing in India, the FVCI route refers to:

answer.text: Registration under SEBI (Foreign Venture Capital Investors) Regulations for direct investment in India

explanation.text: The Logic: The FVCI route is for offshore funds seeking venture-capital investments in eligible unlisted Indian investee companies. It requires SEBI registration under the FVCI Regulations before investment activity, and FVCIs may also acquire units of Category I AIFs (pp. 93, 105-106). The Trap: FDI is subject to sectoral caps and pricing regulations, while FVCI investments are governed by SEBI/FEMA rules and limited to the stipulated areas described in the workbook. The two routes operate under different conditions, not as a free choice on benefit. Note: Use the sourced wording above when comparing the routes - FDI: sectoral caps and pricing; FVCI: SEBI/FEMA rules limited to stipulated areas - rather than informal benefit claims.
